The CreativeID vocabulary.

A handful of Linked Data terms for describing a creative persona, what they've made and who they've made it with, for any practice. They fill the gaps schema.org leaves and mirror the creative lexicons, so a persona published as a file on a website or in a Solid Pod says the same thing as one published to AT Protocol.

namespace https://www.cultureblocs.com/ns/creativeid# · prefix creativeid: · version 0.1, 2026-10-20
also as Turtle and JSON-LD, or ask https://www.cultureblocs.com/ns/creativeid with an Accept header

classes: Persona · Work · Connection · Credit
properties: completionDate · credits · links · subject · relationship · role · note · did · uri · cid
kept on your computer: private · publications · personaId · schemaVersion

How it fits together

A persona file has three kinds of node. The profile is #me, typed both schema:Person and creativeid:Persona. Each work is #work-<id>, typed schema:CreativeWork and creativeid:Work. Each connection is #claim-<id>, a creativeid:Connection. The ids match the AT Protocol record keys, so the same work has the same name everywhere it's published.

{ "@context": { "@vocab": "https://schema.org/", "creativeid": "https://www.cultureblocs.com/ns/creativeid#" }, "@graph": [ { "@id": "#me", "@type": ["Person", "creativeid:Persona"], "name": "Ada Ferrous", "knowsAbout": ["sound", "installation"] }, { "@id": "#work-3l4qkxyz2bc2a", "@type": ["CreativeWork", "creativeid:Work"], "name": "Tidal Room", "creativeid:completionDate": "spring 2024", "creativeid:credits": [{ "@type": "creativeid:Credit", "name": "Jun Okafor", "creativeid:role": "lighting" }] }, { "@id": "#claim-3l4qm2abcd22a", "@type": "creativeid:Connection", "creativeid:subject": { "creativeid:did": "did:web:arches.example", "name": "The Arches" }, "creativeid:relationship": "exhibited" } ] }

Personas made with CreativeID Studio are written this way, and the CreativeID Aggregator reads them from /.well-known/creativeid.jsonld on a website, from a Solid Pod, or as AT Protocol records.

schema.org terms used as they are

Where schema.org already has the right word, CreativeID uses it and adds nothing.

termused onholds
schema:namePersona, Work, Credit, Place, a connection's subjectthe name worked under; a title
schema:descriptionPersona, Workabout; a description
schema:knowsAboutPersonadisciplines, in the creative's own words
schema:homeLocationPersonawhere they're based (a schema:Place)
schema:identifierPersona, Workidentifiers elsewhere (ISNI, ORCID, Wikidata…) as schema:PropertyValue
schema:urlWorkthe work's main page
schema:keywordsWorktags
schema:dateCreated / dateModifiedevery nodewhen the record was first made and last changed (xsd:dateTime)

Classes

creativeid:Persona

A name someone works under, described the way they choose. It is not a legal identity: one person can have several personas, and a duo, band or collective can share one.

Published alongside schema:Person. Personas are never linked to each other in anything published.

AT Protocolcom.cultureblocs.creative.profile
IRIhttps://www.cultureblocs.com/ns/creativeid#Persona

creativeid:Work

Something a persona made, performed, showed, curated or released: an object, an event, a recording, an exhibition, a text.

Published alongside schema:CreativeWork. Saying it is yours is the claim; nobody has to approve it.

kind ofschema:CreativeWork
AT Protocolcom.cultureblocs.creative.work
IRIhttps://www.cultureblocs.com/ns/creativeid#Work

creativeid:Connection

One persona's own statement about a party or a record: I performed at, exhibited with, curated, am a member of, am represented by. It is one-sided by design.

When the other side makes the matching statement, a reader can see that the two agree. A connection without a match is ordinary, not doubtful.

AT Protocolcom.cultureblocs.creative.connection
IRIhttps://www.cultureblocs.com/ns/creativeid#Connection

creativeid:Credit

A name on a work: who else was involved, optionally with their DID and what they did.

AT Protocolcom.cultureblocs.defs#creditRef
IRIhttps://www.cultureblocs.com/ns/creativeid#Credit

Properties

creativeid:completionDate

When the work was made or first shown, in the creator's own words: “2019”, “spring 2024”, “2021–2023”.

Deliberately free text, because creative dates are often approximate or spans. schema:dateCreated is kept for when the record itself was made.

used oncreativeid:Work
valuetext
AT Protocolcreative.work · completionDate
IRIhttps://www.cultureblocs.com/ns/creativeid#completionDate

creativeid:credits

The people and groups credited on a work.

used oncreativeid:Work
valuecreativeid:Credit
AT Protocolcreative.work · credits
IRIhttps://www.cultureblocs.com/ns/creativeid#credits

creativeid:links

Web pages about a persona or a work: a portfolio, a shop, a gallery page, a review. Each is a schema:WebPage with a url and an optional name.

Not schema:sameAs, which would say the page is the persona; not schema:url, which holds one main address.

used oncreativeid:Persona, creativeid:Work
valueschema:WebPage
AT Protocolcreative.profile / creative.work · links
IRIhttps://www.cultureblocs.com/ns/creativeid#links

creativeid:subject

Who or what a connection is about. Either a party, given by creativeid:did (and optionally a name), or a specific record, given by creativeid:uri (and optionally creativeid:cid).

used oncreativeid:Connection
AT Protocolcreative.connection · subject
IRIhttps://www.cultureblocs.com/ns/creativeid#subject

creativeid:relationship

What the connection says, as a short word or phrase.

Suggested values: created, collaborated_on, performed, exhibited, curated, released, represented_by, attests_to, references, member_of. Any other value is valid; a practice that needs a new word doesn’t need a schema change.

used oncreativeid:Connection
valuetext
AT Protocolcreative.connection · relationship
IRIhttps://www.cultureblocs.com/ns/creativeid#relationship

creativeid:role

The part someone played, in their own words: “vocals”, “lighting design”, “co-curator”.

used oncreativeid:Connection, creativeid:Credit
valuetext
AT Protocolcreative.connection · role; defs#creditRef · role
IRIhttps://www.cultureblocs.com/ns/creativeid#role

creativeid:note

A short free-text note on a connection.

used oncreativeid:Connection
valuetext
AT Protocolcreative.connection · note
IRIhttps://www.cultureblocs.com/ns/creativeid#note

creativeid:did

The decentralised identifier (DID) of a party: a persona's AT Protocol account, a venue, a collective. Written as an IRI, e.g. did:plc:… or did:web:…

Also used on the subject of a connection. A DID is what lets a reader match two sides of a connection.

used oncreativeid:Credit, schema:Place
valuean IRI
AT Protocoldefs#didRef / #creditRef / #placeRef · did
IRIhttps://www.cultureblocs.com/ns/creativeid#did

creativeid:uri

The address of a specific record, normally an at:// URI, used as the subject of a connection about that record.

valuean IRI
AT Protocoldefs#strongRef · uri
IRIhttps://www.cultureblocs.com/ns/creativeid#uri

creativeid:cid

The CID of the record named by creativeid:uri, pinning the exact version that was referred to.

If the record is edited later its CID changes, so a reader can say “changed since confirmed” without anyone having to police it.

valuetext
AT Protocoldefs#strongRef · cid
IRIhttps://www.cultureblocs.com/ns/creativeid#cid

Kept on your computer

These terms appear only in the persona file on the creative's own computer. Nothing published ever contains them; they're defined here so that file describes itself.

creativeid:private

Details the creative keeps for themselves (legal name, agent's phone, anything else). Stored only in the persona file on their computer.

used oncreativeid:Persona
IRIhttps://www.cultureblocs.com/ns/creativeid#private

creativeid:publications

Where and when this persona has been published, so republishing updates the same records.

IRIhttps://www.cultureblocs.com/ns/creativeid#publications

creativeid:personaId

The persona's local identifier and file name in the studio.

IRIhttps://www.cultureblocs.com/ns/creativeid#personaId

creativeid:schemaVersion

The version of the local file format, used to upgrade older files.

valuea whole number
IRIhttps://www.cultureblocs.com/ns/creativeid#schemaVersion

How the vocabulary changes

Terms are only ever added. A published term keeps its IRI and its meaning for good; if one stops being useful it's marked deprecated, with what to use instead, and stays resolvable. Usage hints (schema:domainIncludes, schema:rangeIncludes) are suggestions, not rules, so nothing here makes a published persona invalid. Suggestions and questions go to the CreativeID Studio issues.
